data.content_ref: inline:The target names 'inherits' as the relation kind but then substantiates it entirely via a DETECTION DEPENDENCE: SRC_004's forbidden case needs SRC_005's invariant as the signal whose absence reveals the temporal violation. That is dependence/functional coupling, not inheritance. Inheritance requires SRC_004 to take on SRC_005's invariant or behavior as its own; the text never shows SRC_004 inheriting the invariant — it explicitly says SRC_004's mutation DESTROYS the signal, i.e. negates rather than inherits it. A relation whose mechanism is 'A creates the signal and B destroys it' is contradiction or dependence, and the target's own REFUTED IF (SRC_004 detectable by a different invariant, no inheritance of the detection condition needed) concedes the link is detection-dependence, not inherited behavior. So the covering principle is mislabeled: the named kind does not match the stated mechanism.
